I really wanted to like this game but I just find myself more and more irritated with it as I've come to try, (keyword, try) finishing the final racing event. Car list just doesn't feel as impressive as previous entries, customization for aftermarket parts is severely lacking (No Rocket Bunny kits why?????), multiplayer is in a pretty pathetic state, constant crashing issues and bugs, the list goes on. I've crashed 5 or 6 times today alone just trying to rewrap one of my cars so thats fun. AI feels more bullshit than before too. Oh and track design just feels awful, especially so with the dirt tracks. When I see a jump I shouldn't have to break into it because there was a sharp corner right at the landing point and I, like any other person would, floored it for the jump and now have to basically 180 to hit the narrow af checkpoint. I don't know, perhaps I'm just too picky but I look back at FH3 and compare it to this? FH3 was just a better and more fun game.

I loved FH4, so I thought I'd enjoy the next installment, right? Wrong. This garbage was so hammy I couldn't even enjoy driving around. It felt infuriating to play because the cliché Latin announcer/characters were a total turn-off from a car culture that could've been represented better. The landscape was ridiculous, from misplaced native ruins in a spit of a jungle oasis to miles of depressing arid desert. It's like the developer took the extremes of the geography and mashed it all into a non-sense map. I was also bummed that after years from the FH4 release, the graphics barely progressed besides adding a few third-party features developed in FH4 mods.

The cars were fine. Nothing spectacular. The cars were just fine.

.TBH just wait for a sale on the game and its DLC. It's fun to play as a casual "racer", and it *is* live service in the sense that the rewards for the Festival change weekly (along with tracks used, car and class requirements). It's not hard to get the weekly cars and it makes for an enjoyable driving time-waster. The new synthwave station is pretty great, only 2 songs on it that I don't actively enjoy, but that's not to say they're bad.

"The Forza Experience"
You pay WAY too much for a game that is WAYY to big in size (170GB+..).
You launch the game,
takes for every to load,
finally loads in to menu #1,
you press enter,
takes even longer to load,
menu #2, you press start again,
oh there was an update? "Optimizing for your PC" takes a while,
loads into an even longer load screen,
Finally get in the game (around 10-20 min has passed),
you're forced in a sponsored cut scene and event,
you skip it,
you get in to menu #1 (where you can't change cars, you'd have to press play and then go back),
you press play, and you can finally play.
you drive around after all that time, you're speeding on highway, you drive into the "Forza Arena" zone, there's no pop up or anything asking if I want to join the event or just driving on the road, you get put into the event, you have to go the menu again and quit the event, drive back to where you were and continue
Almost every other player you encounter which isn't many is just AFK or in menu

[EDIT 10.04.2022]

Game is still very broken!

- Horizon Open is completely broken. It's more than a week that there is a glitch that permits some cars to go way faster then the other cars. Devs are not fixing this quickly.
- Online services for convoys and social life is still malfunctioning. This means that you will have often problems to see players in your convoy, that you have to recreate convoys when this happens, and that sometime you will have to start a race with not all the players in your convoy. Also, not all the players are usually visible in your map, some of them will only spawn very close to you.
- Horizon Radios are very limited. Prepare your Spotify playlists if you want more kinds of music in your game.
- VIP benefits are broken. There is a very strong possibility that you could not be able to have those.
- Longevity of the game is very short. Once you complete the story, expect to do always the same things, just like in FH4. Weekly series are very short and only last 2 / 3 hours. Lots of bugs in these challenges too.
- Not enough updates from Playground to refresh and/or fix the game.

For those seeking a casual gaming escape, Forza Horizon 5 is a dynamic and wholesome haven. As a casual gamer, I've found this game to be a refreshing breeze in the world of racing games, despite its share of common issues like rammers in online lobbies.
Despite its critiques and the presence of rammers, I wholeheartedly believe that FH5 stands as the best arcade racing game on the market today. It carves a niche for casual gamers like me, providing an opportunity to unwind and enjoy the thrill of racing without the burden of ultra-competitive gameplay.

Just be prepared that one morning you'll quit the game and your save file will be broken and there will be NO ONE to help you. The support team will tell you how to clear your profile so that you can at least log in to the game, and all 170 hours of progress will simply be deleted. And the fact that you have opened the entire map, collected all the secrets, will simply disappear. A very interesting game, with a multi-billion dollar budget, that stores your saves on its server is unable to save them.

It’s a great game, but it can get boring very quickly. And what’s worse is that with the release of Forza 6, this game will quickly die and be forgotten due to Forza 6’s larger map and newer features. I enjoyed this game (whilst I’m not entirely big on arcade games), it was nice to drive around in some of my favorite cars and make cool liveries. Just wish that in-game communication and getting friends to play with was easier.

If I get bored, I might come back to this (as I do miss driving around and goofing off), but the file size will definitely have me questioning whether or not I should come back lol.

But if you’re looking for a chill driving game to just goof off in and can’t afford for Forza 6, get this game when it’s on a deal. Play some missions to unlock necessary features, go find that one dream car you always wanted and take it for a spin. Be sure to look at all the cool liveries that were made, there’s some really good stuff in there and enjoy it with friends if you can.

I've always liked the idea of racing games, but found their execution far too restrictive and geared towards hardcore car fans.

This is the first racing game I've played that felt accessible and fun to play, regardless of my skill level. It has everything a hardcore fan could want, but it also has space for people like me who just want to drive around and have casual fun. The space is rich with content, and I never felt forced to do anything I wasn't interested in.

It's also very generous with cars and activities to get rewards.

This is probably one of the more detailed non-sim racing games on steam. Granted it's a Triple A title, and has several issues of varying degrees, but for overall visuals, play ability on various devices, and integration game play, this is a strong game.
I'd easily recommend this to anyone who enjoys Arcade-esque racing games, or a very good time with friends, as you upgrade cars, and test both your driving ability, and your tuning patience with each other. Worth it on sale, DLC's are optional, but far from needed for a good time.

Pros:
Arcade
Accessibility
Gameplay with friends
Ease of learning
Visuals are great
Car selection and upgrade-ability

Cons:
Xbox connection issues
Somewhat clunky menu system
No late game realistic shifts in game play or style
Car upgrades and abilities are not fully logical, there are power systems that are out of your control
The course selection is relatively lacking late game, especially in the off-road/dirt department.
The course maker is fairly clunky, but is operable at least.
